summary:
Turn 58 reviewed the codec truncation check, whose outcome is violated.

State on entry. Claim C10-command-value-length-survives-the-wire has one artifact, 4cd03e5aa3ec4080807408f6b3678c14 (executed as ede08d08…), with outcome violated and oracle correspondence unreviewed. Its retained stream shows the round trip: 70013 bytes on the wire for a 70000-byte declared value, 4464 bytes decoded (the value modulo 65536) and only 4477 bytes consumed, with value_matches false.

Review judgement (checker_correspondence, no_issue_found). Requirement versus predicate: the claim is that a value the client can build must survive the codec or be rejected, and the predicate asserts value_matches on the round-trip event, evaluated on the codec's own output with the declared length, decoded length and consumed bytes all printed. Entry and legality: both directions of the codec are the implementation's own and are called directly; the premise that such a value can enter the protocol rests on the command size being a configuration parameter (aws.conf sets 1000 while the field carries up to 65535), and that premise is recorded as a limitation rather than assumed silently. Oracle and observation: value_matches compares the decoded bytes with the payload the harness built, and the wire-length event shows the encoder emitted every byte, so the shortening is attributable to the length field rather than to a truncated write; identity is the shared subject field between prerequisite and result. Limits are explicit: the shipped configuration never reaches the boundary, no replica reader consumes the shifted stream so the desynchronisation's effect on the following message is unobserved, and whether the client library caps the size it builds was not read. No counterevidence was found that the codec preserves values in this scope.

Effect on the run's picture. The finding joins the other implementation-semantics ones as another place where a value the implementation accepts is not faithfully carried — here on the wire rather than in the durable record — with its importance bounded by the configured command size. Audit spec version 12; the nine earlier settled claims (C1/C6/C7/C9 confirmed violations, C2/C3/C4 confirmed, C5/C8 bounded protections) and the two paused candidates are untouched, and the scope-issue bookkeeping on the superseded C1 artifact remains the only visible administrative item. No requirement, premise or earlier observation was weakened.
